dataset_title: Li et al. Sentinel-1 Ocean Phenomena Dataset
citation: Li, X. et al. (2024). A benchmark SAR dataset for ocean phenomena recognition and semantic segmentation.
overlap_precedence_rule: Sequential polygon rasterization in Labelme; subsequent annotations overwrite antecedent pixels. Unannotated ocean pixels default to Class 0 (Background).
ambiguous_boundary_semantics: Multi-look 100m pixel aggregation creates a +/-50m to +/-100m spatial quantization envelope along phenomenon perimeters. Boundaries on 100m grid lack native 10m high-frequency phase and texture support.

classes.physical_definition: Ambient open-ocean sea surface without identifiable discrete atmospheric, oceanic, biogenic, or man-made phenomena under prevailing wind forcing.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Generally distinct from oil slicks under moderate wind (>3 m/s); low-wind sub-patches in unannotated background may trigger residual false alarms.
classes.recommended_action: Retain as multi-class background (ID 0) in OPS-01 segmentation.

classes.physical_definition: Synoptic-scale or mesoscale boundary separating distinct air masses, producing sharp surface wind speed/direction steps and distinct radar backscatter transitions.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Linear wind-shift boundaries occasionally exhibit narrow low-wind shear zones that can be misidentified as linear oil slicks.

classes.physical_definition: Surface-active biogenic organic films produced by marine phytoplankton blooms, zooplankton excretion, or fish spawning that damp capillary and short gravity waves via Marangoni elasticity.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Primary global false-positive generator for radar oil detection; exhibits identical radiometric damping properties in single-pol SAR without collateral chlorophyll data.
classes.recommended_action: Mandatory inclusion in OPS-01; critical for discriminative oil vs look-alike reasoning.

classes.physical_definition: Drifting glacial freshwater ice bodies in polar/subpolar waters, displaying bright dihedral specular corner reflection with distinct down-range radar shadows.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Bright point/volume targets; radar shadows behind giant icebergs can theoretically cause naive dark-patch triggers but are morphologically distinct.
classes.recommended_action: Retain in OPS-01 cryospheric mode; exclude from tropical/temperate oil spill benchmarks.

classes.physical_definition: Calm ocean sectors where 10m surface wind speed drops below ~2.5-3.0 m/s threshold required to generate short Bragg resonance waves, yielding near-zero radar backscatter.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Ubiquitous physical cause of false alarms across global SAR surveillance; produces massive low-dB regions resembling extensive oil slicks.
classes.recommended_action: Mandatory inclusion in OPS-01; primary benchmark look-alike target.

classes.physical_definition: Atmospheric boundary-layer convective organization forming open or closed polygonal cells (10-50 km diameter) that modulate sea surface wind stress in cellular patterns.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Divergent calm centers within open convection cells produce dark patches; recognizable by characteristic honeycomb spatial periodicity.
classes.recommended_action: Include in OPS-01 general ocean phenomena recognition.

classes.physical_definition: Sharp boundary between water masses differing in temperature, salinity, or density, characterized by horizontal velocity shear and surface convergence collecting surfactants.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Surface convergence bands trap surfactants into narrow, winding dark lines that strongly mimic linear oil seepage or bilge dumps.
classes.recommended_action: Include in OPS-01 priority look-alike evaluation.

classes.physical_definition: Small-scale, intense maritime cyclone forming over high-latitude oceans poleward of the polar front, displaying spiral cloud/wind bands.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: High-latitude storm feature; high wind regimes dominate, but inner eye-like calm cores can generate localized low-backscatter features.
classes.recommended_action: Optional in general OPS-01; isolate to subpolar regional models.

classes.physical_definition: Localized convective precipitating cells where downdrafts hit the sea surface causing divergence, turbulence, and raindrop ring waves, producing dark centers and bright splash rims.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Downdraft footprints produce sharp, irregularly shaped dark patches that frequently trigger automated dark-spot detectors in tropical and humid zones.
classes.recommended_action: Mandatory inclusion in OPS-01 multi-phenomenon training.

classes.physical_definition: Frozen seawater covering high-latitude marine surfaces in various stages of development (grease ice, nilas, pancake ice, pack ice, fast ice).
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Early-stage grease ice and dark nilas damp surface capillary waves, presenting severe radiometric look-alike properties in Arctic/Antarctic monitoring.
classes.recommended_action: Segregate into polar evaluation tier; do not mix into non-polar oil benchmarks.

classes.physical_definition: Quasi-parallel linear roughness streaks on the sea surface aligned with the boundary-layer wind direction, caused by helical roll vortices or Langmuir circulation cells.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Alternating low-roughness streaks can be confused with multiple parallel oil windrows, but periodic regular spacing assists discrimination.
classes.recommended_action: Include in OPS-01 boundary layer feature set.

classes.physical_definition: Rotating mesoscale/sub-mesoscale oceanic vortex whose surface current shears entrain biogenic surfactants into conspicuous spiral arms.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Surfactant spiral slicks are visually striking and easily confused with long twisting oil slicks by automated detectors.
classes.recommended_action: Include in OPS-01 core ocean phenomenon recognition.

classes.physical_definition: Subsurface solitary wave packets traveling along internal oceanic density stratification (pycnocline), modulating surface currents into paired convergence (bright) and divergence (dark) bands.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: The dark divergence bands accumulate surface films, creating curved parallel dark stripes that trigger alarms along continental shelves and straits.
classes.recommended_action: Mandatory inclusion in OPS-01; iconic oceanic hydrodynamic signature.

classes.physical_definition: Artificial metallic structures including merchant vessels, fishing vessels, and offshore oil/gas platforms displaying high radar cross-section (RCS) specular returns.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: Extremely bright point targets; not confused with dark slicks, but essential for detecting discharging vessels and offshore infrastructure attribution.
classes.recommended_action: Retain in multi-task OPS-01; vessel context directly enables oil spill attribution.

classes.physical_definition: Surface hydrocarbon mineral oil contamination from shipping discharges, well blowouts, or pipeline leaks.
classes.lookalike_risk_assessment: The primary positive target of oil spill detection. In Li et al., annotations were collected from historical literature/news reports without standardized in-situ chemical verification.
classes.recommended_action: Isolate from look-alike evaluation; do not treat Li OS as independent test ground truth without explicit qualification.
